# build_man_pages

[← Command index](README.md)

Generate the command reference in Docs from every command's help text.

## Synopsis

```text
build_man_pages [options]
```

## Description

Builds the parser of each command in `[project.scripts]` and renders a page from it:
the description, every option with its default and allowed values, and the details,
examples, notes and see-also the command declares. The pages are never edited by
hand, so the help text is the only thing to maintain.

Parsers are built against a throwaway home directory holding only the default
JoyBox.ini, so nothing from your own configuration ends up in a default shown on a page.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Directory to write the pages into, instead of Docs/reference/man in this checkout. |
| `-s, --project_path <project_path>` | pyproject.toml whose commands to document, instead of this checkout's. |
| `-k, --check` | Report out-of-date pages and incomplete help text without writing anything. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Regenerate every page

```bash
build_man_pages
```

### Fail if a page is out of date or a command's help text is incomplete

```bash
build_man_pages --check
```

## Notes

- A page for a command that no longer exists is removed.
- `--check` exits non-zero and writes nothing, which makes it usable in a hook or CI.
